about: Hand-authored X-E2 4.11 service-capture facts for fujimod-xe2-capture. Not generated. A fact is used only when its value is present and its confidence is high; any other fact makes the tool refuse the steps that need it and name the fact.

service_usb.evidence: Firmware: two USB device descriptors (bLength 0x12, bcdUSB 0x0200, bMaxPacketSize0 0x40, idVendor 0x04cb, idProduct 0xff80, bcdDevice 0x0100) in decoded stream-0032025c at 0x0146bfc0 and 0x0146bfd4. Hardware: owner's X-E2 enumerated on Windows as USB\VID_04CB&PID_FF80 after selector UP + full shutter at power-on with USB connected (BOARD.md, Owner camera test, 2026-11-18).

product.evidence: catalog/firmware/xe2/4.11/bulk.generated.json and execution.generated.json `product`, written by the upstream locator (generation.generated.json: xe2-411 bulk available).

value.usb_condition: USB cable connected to the PC before switching ON; rear LED solid green

entry.evidence: Owner hardware test, not firmware analysis (BOARD.md, Owner camera test). U9 found no main-firmware code that samples these keys at power-on, so the check is presumably in the boot ROM or loader.

code_checks.evidence: All 15 bulk.generated.json code_checks, the 8 upload code_checks and the 4096-byte mapped_probe were re-hashed by U10 against the streams decoded from FWUP0004.DAT (sha256 d324e147...ca99bb7) with fujimod.firmware.scan/decode: 24/24 sha256 match. The tool checks the 15 bulk code_checks on the camera before any write.

read_gate.evidence: Still unlocated for xe2-411 (U11): no X-E2 code directly shows the debug-read gate offset/enabled value, so it must not be guessed or borrowed. U11 decoded the two A32 exec streams from FWUP0004.DAT (sha256 d324e147…; stream-0016025c base 0x8a0400, stream-0032025c base 0xf6a9c0, hashes match firmware.json) and located the FF80 vendor-command infrastructure in stream-0032025c: USB device descriptors 04cb:ff80 at 0x146bfc0/0x146bfd4; the (command,timeout) table at 0x146c004 (0x550001/0x760001/0x450006 = 1000 ms, 0x660002 = 60000 ms); the vendor-command handler-pointer table at 0x146c024 (29 real handlers at 0x10c9xxx-0x10cfxxx, default/unsupported handler 0x10cf7e0 returning status word 0x2005); the request parser at 0x10c89c0 that copies up to 4 command args into the RAM struct at 0x154335c; and the service-session state struct at 0x15434f0. The specific 200001/function-2 (read_memory) handler that consults the configuration-RAM gate byte, and the enabled constant it compares against, were NOT isolated to the 'X-E2 code directly shows the value' bar. The X70-family debug offset 0xf7 (crates/workflows/src/flash/exr2.rs: configuration_flags reads [0xa3,0xf7], require flags[1]==1) is NOT borrowed; a single `ldrb rX,[rY,#0xf7]` at 0x126d5f0 is unverified as the gate. Needs the external x70view service-workflow locator, or completion of the 200001-handler trace below. U14 (emulator trace, Opus): could NOT run the X-E2 4.11 firmware in the repo's emulator on this machine, so no handler behavior was observed and the fact stays null. All three bring-up paths are blocked: (A) native boot (fujimod-emulator-boot open_exr2 / `fujimod-emulator boot`) refuses xe2-411 at prepared() because its configurations/emulator/xe2-411/run.json declares inputs/scene/execution = null ('configuration xe2-411 declares no startup inputs', reproduced with and without the xe2-411-browser-usb overlay); and open_exr2 verifies a 16 KiB boot-ROM file by sha256 4ecedfbfc1910bde488d36abe4380621f8845e6afcfc6cf54a49a33ec0abf9be ('--boot-rom ... ROM dump is required'), which is absent everywhere on this machine (same ROM U0 reported missing). (B) web/wasm simulated camera (apps/web/src/dev-tools/simulated-camera.ts WasmEngine) needs a prebuilt per-firmware USB wasm bundle (firmware.emulate.usb.bundle + wasm.json) — none on the machine, no `emulate` facts in catalog/generation.generated.json — plus a physical_controls.boot.service entry for xe2 (absent, U9) and the wasm/nightly toolchain (unavailable, U0). (C) no in-repo fixture runs the real firmware answering FF80: the usb-app80 FF80 tests drive a scripted transport (crates/usb/src/testing.rs Script), not an emulated board. Invoking the 0x200001 handler directly on a bare exr2 board would execute it against uninitialized configuration RAM / no service session, so it could not demonstrate the gate changing behavior (step-4 bar) and would be a large new harness the task forbids. Unicorn CPU + emulator crates do build/run here; the blocker is firmware bring-up inputs, not execution.

reset_guard.evidence: Still unlocated for xe2-411 (U11): no X-E2 code directly shows the reset-guard offset or its value, so it must not be guessed or borrowed. This is the configuration-RAM byte that stops the stock service-mode teardown from restoring defaults (`guard.offset`, `guard.value` must be 1). U11 did not isolate the teardown routine that honors it; firmware does contain a `service_command` sender at 0x10F4BA8 (restart.generated.json; U9) whose in-session sub-command senders are at 0x10F4C28..0x10F5914, but the specific shutdown path that reads the guard byte was not pinned. The X70-family guard offset 0xa3 (crates/workflows/src/flash/build.rs) is NOT borrowed; `ldrb …,#0xa3` is a very common struct access in these streams (dozens of sites) and is not decisive. The guard's state words, callback table, aliases and output-state checks (service-workflow `guard`) are also not located. U14 (emulator trace, Opus): the dynamic emulator trace could not be run (the X-E2 4.11 firmware cannot be brought up in the repo's emulator on this machine — see the read_gate evidence for the three blocked paths: native boot refuses xe2-411 for null startup inputs and requires the absent 16 KiB boot ROM, the web/wasm simulated camera has no prebuilt bundle/catalog facts/service controls/toolchain, and no in-repo fixture runs the firmware answering FF80), so the service-mode teardown guard read was not observed and the fact stays null.

slow_read_bytes.evidence: Still unlocated for xe2-411 (U11): the largest FF80 0x200001 read the firmware accepts per command (`configuration.memory_read_bytes`, tool bound 1..=4096). It is the size-limit comparison inside the same 200001/function-2 debug-read handler as read_gate, which U11 did not isolate from the handler table at 0x146c024 (see read_gate evidence). No size bound was derived from X-E2 code, so it is left null rather than assumed. U14 (emulator trace, Opus): the per-read size bound is applied inside the same 0x200001 handler as read_gate, which was not exercised because the X-E2 4.11 firmware could not be brought up in the repo's emulator on this machine (see the read_gate evidence for the three blocked bring-up paths), so no bound was observed and the fact stays null.

flash_reader.evidence: No reviewed EXR II reader image is pinned yet, so the flash backup refuses. Owner-approved mechanism (U13, 2026-11-18): the existing transport `exr2-query-heap` (fujimod_workflows::flash::backup / flash/exr2.rs, as Dev Tools uses on the X70) uploads a reader to a stock heap block in camera RAM, runs it from the diagnostic-query callback, and cleans up; nothing is written to flash or stored. The repo holds that host-side path and the xe2-411 flash contract (flash.generated.json: 128 MiB raw NAND, nand_read_transfer, control sha256), but NOT a reader image: build::prepare_exr2 links one from an externally compiled reader (flash_reader_call, flash_reader, flash_reader_progress symbols) plus the corpus exr2_execution locator, and neither the reader source nor a staged flash-reader.json/.bin for any body is checked in. To pin one: build it with the flash_reader_build example from reviewed source, put the artifact JSON and image beside this file, and set value {mechanism, artifact, artifact_sha256, image, image_sha256, image_bytes, review} with confidence high; build.rs then verifies both hashes and the static screen (src/reader_scan.rs) or fails the build. The step also needs read_gate, reset_guard and slow_read_bytes located, with read_gate/reset_guard agreeing with the offsets the reused path reads (0xf7 = 1, 0xa3).
